events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The cancellation came from the driver, not the rider: the timeline records acceptance at 22:37:00 and cancellation by the driver at 22:45:05, with $6.61 charged on record [F4][F7][NS-0]. Under NS-0 the fee can therefore only stand through the driver-side no-show branch NS-1, which is conjunctive: the driver must have tapped "I'm Here" (i), been within the pickup radius at that moment (ii), and waited more than 3 minutes there until cancelling (iii) [F4][NS-1].

Element (i) fails on the record. The chat and timeline show the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null) [F6], and the driver's own post-trip statement admits it: "I forgot to press the I'm Here button but I was there" [F12]. The driver advocate concedes the same [F6][F12][NS-1]. With (i) unsatisfied the fee cannot be retained, and NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full [F7][NS-2]. The amount is the fee recorded as charged, $6.61 [F7][F4], distributed per NS-7.

The driver's physical presence is genuine — closest approach 33 m at 22:41:00, first inside 200 m at 22:39:45, 5 min 20 s cumulative inside the radius, and 4 min 0 s stationary at 38 m from 22:41:05 to 22:45:05 [F1][F2][F3][F5]. That satisfies the substance of NS-1 (ii)/(iii), but NS-1 is conjunctive, so a real wait on the ground cannot cure the missing tap [F6][F2][F3][NS-1]. The driver's chat message at 22:41 ("At the pickup point") and at 22:44 ("Waited 4 min, cancelling") and the complete, fully timestamped two-message record [F9][F10][F11] show he communicated but never performed the required arrival confirmation.

No account flag follows. The NS-2 flag attaches only when the driver taps "I'm Here" while GPS shows him away from the pickup; here GPS places him 33–38 m away at all material times and no tap occurred at all [F6][F1][F2][F3][NS-2]. what_would_change: Had NS-1 (i) held ((i) arrival confirmed: driver tapped I'm Here, or the platform auto-confirmed arrival), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver's own statement admits he never tapped the "I'm Here" button; the system timeline confirms this — the driver_pressed_here_at field is null — so NS-1 (i) fails and the $6.61 cancellation fee does not stand.
Because the fee's precondition in NS-1 (i) is unmet, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full, refund_full of the exact amount recorded as charged.

The driver cancelled, not the rider (the rider never cancelled), so the fee can only be justified through the driver-side no-show branch NS-1/NS-2 — and that branch fails; NS-3 confirms a driver cancellation without a valid NS-1 no-show leaves the rider owing nothing.

Even if the driver had pressed "I'm Here", the 200 m/wait conditions are only just met and the wait of 4 min 0 s stationary (22:41:05–22:45:05) at 38 m from pickup began only at 22:41:05, so the driver's "waited 4 min" message is measured from a point after his own arrival notice, showing the timing was tight rather than a clear-cut no-show; the rider was en route at the time.

The chat record is complete and fully timestamped, so the consent/timing facts needed to resolve this case are available and the case does not fall into the evidence-gap escalation of G12; the only thing the driver offers beyond the system record is his post-hoc assertion that he forgot the button — a claim, not a system record.

The driver pressed "I'm Here" nowhere in the record yet charged/reported a no-show, which is the abuse-of-cancellation-and-waiting-button pattern Ryde lists as a flaggable account matter; this is offered only as an additional account-review request, not as the finding.

weaknesses: The GPS record cuts against us on the wait element: F2 shows the driver first entered the 200 m zone at 22:39:45 with 5 min 20 s cumulative inside it, and F5 records platform arrival at 22:39:45 with cancellation 5 min 20 s later — i.e. the NS-1 (ii) and (iii) elements (within 200 m and > 3 min waiting) are met, so the driver will argue only the missing button tap is a technicality and the no-show was genuine.

F1 and F3 show the driver was genuinely 33–38 m from the pickup point and stationary there for a full 4 minutes, so the driver can argue his F12 statement is corroborated by GPS as to physical presence, and that our client did not board during that window.

Our client's own complaint says only "I was on my way down" (no fact id supports an arrival time), and no fact shows the rider was at or near the pickup point, so the rider cannot show she was there or about to be there within the driver's wait.
The driver's profile (F17: 4.69 rating, 770 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days) will be used to argue this is an isolated administrative slip, not the abuse pattern in C6.

claims.assertion: The driver reached the pick-up area and was physically present: GPS puts him within 200 m of the pick-up point from 22:39:45, with a closest approach of 33 m at 22:41:00, and he stood stationary 38 m from the pick-up point from 22:41:05 to 22:45:05 — a real, sustained presence, not a remote cancellation.

The driver waited long enough on the ground for a no-show: cumulative time within 200 m of the pick-up before cancellation was 5 min 20 s, and 4 min 0 s of that was stationary at 38 m, both well over the 3-minute threshold contemplated by NS-1(iii).

The rider was never seen at the pick-up point for the whole wait — the driver's message at 22:41 states he is at the pick-up point and no chat message from the rider shows them arriving or asking for more time before the cancellation at 22:45:05.

The only formal defect is procedural, not factual: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), as he himself concedes in his statement, so the $6.61 cannot be retained as a matter of strict rule and the passenger-side remedy under NS-2 follows even though the underlying no-show conduct was real.

This is an isolated lapse by an otherwise clean driver: 2.9 years on the platform, 4.69 rating, 770 trips in 90 days, zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in 90 days, so nothing supports a fraud-flag for abuse of the arrival/cancellation button.

Neither side's account suggests any threat, harassment, intimidation or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is triggered — the driver simply completed his wait and cancelled.

weaknesses: The controlling clause NS-1 requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here", and the timeline fact F6 shows he never did; NS-2 then mandates a full refund of the $6.61 and the rider's complaint is grounded squarely on that.

The wait F3 measured by GPS is 4 min 0 s (22:41:05–22:45:05) while the driver's own chat message F10 says "Waited 4 min", and the timeline arrival is 22:39:45 — the rider will argue the driver cancelled at the earliest lawful moment rather than giving the rider a fair opportunity, and there is no evidence the driver contacted the rider beyond the two one-way messages F9/F10.

The rider's complaint states he was "on my way down"; the chat record F11 confirms the record is complete and contains no rider message, but the rider will argue the driver never made clear contact, weakening the driver's no-show narrative.

points.response: We do not contest physical presence — F1/F2/F3 do show the driver near the point — but presence is only NS-1 (ii); NS-1 requires (i) the "I'm Here" tap as well, and F6 shows driver_pressed_here_at is null, so D1 cannot establish the fee even if every other element is true.

The wait element of NS-1 (iii) may be satisfied — F2 (5 min 20 s within 200 m) and F3 (4 min 0 s stationary) sit above 3:01 — but NS-1 is conjunctive: (i) and (ii) and (iii) must all hold, and (i) fails on F6, so long waiting time cannot cure the missing button tap.

The absence of a rider chat message proves nothing about the rider's whereabouts: F11 shows the chat is a complete, fully timestamped record of two one-way driver messages (F9, F10) with no message from the driver asking the rider to come out or confirming contact, and no fact shows the rider was not en route; "not seen in chat" is not "no-show".

Conceded as to the outcome — this is exactly our case: F6 shows no "I'm Here" tap (as the driver admits at F12), so under NS-1 the conditions are not fulfilled and NS-2 requires full refund of the $6.61 recorded at F7; we simply note that calling the unmet statutory precondition "procedural" is the whole reason the fee falls.

We accept the driver has a clean record (F17) and we do not press a fraud flag as the basis of the case; the flag we raised in C6 was offered only as an ancillary account-review request (NS-6/RD-6 style additional action), and dropping it does not affect the refund that NS-2 independently requires on F6.
We agree: nothing in F9, F10 or F12 reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation arises and this case can be decided on the ordinary NS rules.

Conceded in substance: the timeline fact F6 shows driver_pressed_here_at is null and the driver's statement F12 admits it, so NS-1(i) is not met on the record; I do not contest that the $6.61 cannot be retained under NS-1. My brief already asks for refund_full of $6.61 (F7) for exactly this reason — the dispute is only about whether this was fraud or a forgotten tap.

Not contested as to outcome — refund_full of $6.61 (the amount recorded as charged, F7, F4) is what the driver asks for; the rider's claim adds nothing to my brief. Note that a refund under NS-2 does not require a finding that the driver was elsewhere, and the GPS facts F1/F2/F3 show he was 33-38 m away and stationary for 4 min 0 s.

Accepted that the cancellation was driver-initiated (F4), so NS-3's outcome (rider owes no cancellation fee) follows with the refund; but NS-3 also records that the cancellation counts against the driver's rate as an account matter, not that the no-show was fabricated — the system facts F1/F2/F3 show the driver really did wait at the pickup point.

The timing is not "only just" met: F2 records 5 min 20 s cumulative inside 200 m from 22:39:45, and F3 records a continuous 4 min 0 s stationary at 38 m, both above the 3-minute measure in NS-1(iii); the rider's "I was on my way down" has no fact id behind it, and the complete chat record F11 contains no rider message at all during the 5 min 20 s wait.

Accepted: the chat record is complete and timestamped (F11), so no G12 evidence gap applies and the case is decidable; the rider is right that F12 is a post-hoc statement, but it is corroborated on the material point of physical presence by GPS facts F1, F2 and F3.

The abuse pattern in NS-2 requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here" while GPS shows him outside the pickup area (F6 shows he pressed it at no time and F1/F2/F3 show he was inside 200 m), and the profile F17 records 2.9 years, 770 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes upheld in 90 days, so a fraud flag is not supportable; my brief seeks refund only, with no flag.
